steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease two 9-inch round pans.
Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy, then beat in eggs one at a time, followed by vanilla.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt together; add to the batter alternately with milk until just combined.
Divide batter between pans and bake 25-30 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat frosting butter, cocoa, powdered sugar, and milk together until fluffy, then frost between layers and over the top.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and generously grease a 10-cup bundt pan.
Cream butter and sugar, then beat in eggs one at a time until smooth.
Fold in flour and cocoa powder until just combined, then stir in walnuts.
Pour into the bundt pan and bake 50-60 minutes — the center should look slightly underdone. Do not overbake or the tunnel disappears.
Cool in the pan 1-2 hours, invert onto a plate, then drizzle with a milk-thinned powdered sugar glaze.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease three 8-inch round pans.
Whisk flour, sugar, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt together.
Stir in oil and eggs until just combined, then fold in banana, pineapple, and pecans — do not overmix.
Divide between pans and bake 25 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat cream cheese, butter, and powdered sugar together and frost between layers and over the top; garnish with extra pecans.

4 tbsp ground flaxseed + 12 tbsp water, rested 5 min

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease two 9-inch round pans.
Whisk flour, sugar, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt together.
Stir in oil and eggs, then fold in carrots, pineapple, and walnuts.
Divide between pans and bake 30-35 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat cream cheese, butter, and powdered sugar together and frost between layers and over the top.
Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F) and butter four ramekins, dusting with cocoa powder.
Melt chocolate and butter together until smooth.
Whisk eggs, egg yolks, and sugar until pale and thick, then fold in the melted chocolate.
Fold in flour and salt just until combined, then divide among the ramekins.
Bake 10-12 minutes until the edges are set but the center still jiggles. Unmold immediately and serve.

1 tbsp ground flaxseed + 3 tbsp water, rested 5 min

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and line a 12-cup muffin tin.
Whisk flour, cocoa, baking soda, and salt together.
In a separate bowl, whisk oil, buttermilk, egg, food coloring, and vinegar, then combine with the dry ingredients.
Divide batter among liners and bake 18-20 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat cream cheese, butter, and powdered sugar together and pipe onto the cooled cupcakes.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease four 6-inch round pans.
Cream butter and sugar, beat in eggs and vanilla, then alternate adding the flour/baking powder mix with milk.
Divide batter evenly and tint each portion a different color, then pour into pans and bake 22-25 minutes.
Cool completely, then stack and crumb-coat the layers with vanilla buttercream, chilling between coats.
Warm the cream and pour over the white chocolate to make ganache; once slightly cooled, drip it down the sides of the chilled cake.
Preheat oven to 230°C (450°F) and line a 9-inch springform pan with overlapping parchment that extends well above the rim.
Beat cream cheese and sugar until smooth, then add eggs one at a time.
Mix in heavy cream, salt, and flour until just combined — do not overmix.
Pour into the pan and bake 50-55 minutes until deeply browned on top and the center still wobbles.
Cool at room temperature, then chill at least 4 hours before releasing from the pan.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a 9x13-inch pan.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt together.
Beat eggs and sugar until pale and doubled in volume, mix in melted butter and vanilla, then fold in the dry ingredients.
Pour into the pan and bake 25 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely, then poke holes all over the top.
Whisk whole milk, evaporated milk, and condensed milk together and pour slowly over the cake, letting it soak in.
Chill at least 2 hours, then top with whipped cream just before serving.
Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). Melt the caramel sugar in a saucepan until deep amber, then pour into the bottom of a bundt pan and swirl to coat.
Blend condensed milk, evaporated milk, cream cheese, flan eggs, and vanilla until smooth — this is the flan batter.
Whisk flour, cocoa, cake sugar, baking powder, and baking soda together, then mix in oil, cake eggs, and milk until smooth — this is the cake batter.
Pour the cake batter over the caramel in the pan, then gently pour the flan batter on top without stirring — they'll swap places as they bake.
Cover tightly with foil and set the pan in a larger roasting pan filled with hot water halfway up the sides. Bake 60-70 minutes until set.
Cool completely, then chill at least 4 hours before inverting onto a plate.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease three 8-inch round pans.
Cream butter and sugar, beat in eggs one at a time, then vanilla and almond extract.
Alternate adding flour/baking powder with milk until just combined. Divide between pans and bake 20-25 minutes. Cool completely.
Simmer syrup sugar and water into a light syrup, then brush over each cooled layer.
Whisk egg whites and frosting sugar over a double boiler until warm, then whip to stiff peaks. Beat in frosting butter a little at a time until smooth meringue buttercream forms.
Frost between layers and over the outside of the cake.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease an 8-inch springform pan.
Whisk melted butter, sugar, eggs, and vanilla together.
Fold in flour, cocoa, and salt until just combined.
Pour into the pan and bake 20 minutes — the center should still be very soft and underbaked.
Cool slightly, dust with powdered sugar, and serve with whipped cream.
Warm honey, sugar, and butter together in a saucepan until melted, then whisk in baking soda — it will foam up.
Remove from heat, whisk in eggs, then stir in flour until a soft dough forms. Divide into 8 portions and roll each thin.
Bake each layer at 175°C (350°F) for 4-5 minutes until golden; trim edges while warm and reserve the trimmings.
Whip sour cream, powdered sugar, and heavy cream together into a frosting.
Stack the layers with frosting between each, frost the outside, then press the reserved crumbs onto the sides.
Refrigerate at least 8 hours, ideally overnight, so the layers soften into a torte before serving.
Mix flour, salt, yeast, and warm water into a smooth dough. Let rise 1 hour until doubled.
Roll out the dough and enclose the cold butter block, then fold and roll repeatedly as you would puff pastry, sprinkling sugar between folds and chilling between each to keep the butter firm.
After the final fold, roll out and cut into squares, fold the corners into the center, and place in a muffin tin, sprinkling more sugar on top.
Proof 45 minutes, then bake at 220°C (425°F) for 20-25 minutes until deeply caramelized and shattering-crisp on the outside.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a 9-inch springform pan.
Melt the dark chocolate and butter together. Beat egg yolks with half the sugar until pale, then whisk into the chocolate mixture.
Whip egg whites with the remaining sugar to soft peaks, then fold into the batter along with the flour.
Bake 45-50 minutes until a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs. Cool completely.
Slice the cake in half horizontally, spread warmed apricot jam between the layers and over the top and sides.
Warm the glaze cream, pour over the glaze chocolate and stir smooth, then pour over the cake, letting it drip down the sides. Let set before slicing.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a loaf pan.
Cream butter, sugar, and mawa together until smooth, then beat in eggs one at a time.
Fold in flour, baking powder, cardamom, and nutmeg, alternating with milk.
Pour into the pan and bake 40-45 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Preheat oven to 165°C (325°F). Whisk flour, baking powder, and half the sugar together.
Whisk in egg yolks, coconut milk, oil, and pandan extract until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whip egg whites with cream of tartar, gradually adding the remaining sugar, to stiff peaks.
Fold the egg whites into the batter in three additions, then pour into an ungreased tube pan.
Bake 45-50 minutes until springy to the touch. Invert the pan immediately and cool completely upside down before releasing.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a baking pan.
Mix semolina, coconut, sugar, yogurt, melted butter, and baking powder into a thick batter.
Spread into the pan, score into diamonds, and press an almond into the center of each piece.
Bake 30-35 minutes until golden.
Simmer syrup sugar, water, lemon juice, and orange blossom water into a syrup, then pour the hot syrup over the cake as soon as it comes out of the oven.
Preheat oven to 160°C (320°F) and prepare a water bath. Melt cream cheese, butter, and milk together until smooth.
Whisk in egg yolks, flour, cornstarch, and lemon juice.
In a separate bowl, whip egg whites with cream of tartar, gradually adding sugar, to soft peaks.
Fold the egg whites into the cheese mixture in three additions.
Pour into a lined pan, place in the water bath, and bake 65-70 minutes until golden and just set.
Turn off the oven and let the cake cool inside with the door ajar to prevent sinking.
Preheat oven to 160°C (320°F) and line a loaf pan with parchment extending above the rim.
Whisk eggs and sugar over a warm water bath until warm to the touch and doubled in volume.
Whisk in honey and milk, then fold in the bread flour in three additions.
Pour into the pan, tap firmly on the counter to release air bubbles, and bake 50-55 minutes.
Drop the pan from a small height as soon as it comes out of the oven to prevent shrinking, then cool wrapped in plastic to keep it moist.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a 9x13-inch pan.
Mix base flour, base sugar, base butter, base egg, and baking powder into a soft dough and press evenly into the pan.
Beat cream cheese and topping butter until smooth, add topping eggs and vanilla, then beat in powdered sugar until smooth.
Pour the topping over the base.
Bake 40-45 minutes until the edges are golden but the center still jiggles slightly — it should never fully set.
Cool completely before slicing; dust with powdered sugar.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease three 8-inch pans.
Whisk flour, sugar, cocoa, baking soda, baking powder, and salt together.
Whisk in eggs, buttermilk, oil, and hot coffee until smooth — the batter will be thin.
Divide between pans and bake 22-25 minutes. Cool completely, then crumble one layer into fine crumbs for coating.

Whisk pudding sugar, pudding cocoa, and cornstarch in a saucepan, whisk in pudding milk and egg yolks, and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened into a pudding. Stir in pudding butter, then chill.
Stack the two remaining cake layers with pudding filling between them and on top, then press the reserved crumbs over the entire outside.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease three 9-inch pans.
Cream butter and sugar, alternate adding flour/baking powder with milk, then fold in whipped egg whites and vanilla.
Divide between pans and bake 20-25 minutes. Cool completely.
Cook filling egg yolks, filling sugar, and filling butter over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened. Remove from heat and stir in bourbon, pecans, and cherries.
Spread the filling between the layers only, leaving the outside of the cake bare in the traditional style. Let set before slicing.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a baking dish.
Beat sugar and egg until light, then mix in melted butter and apricot jam.
Whisk baking soda into vinegar — it will fizz — then add to the batter alternately with flour and milk.
Pour into the dish and bake 35-40 minutes until golden and set.
Warm sauce cream, sauce butter, and sauce sugar together until the butter melts, then pour the hot sauce evenly over the pudding as soon as it comes out of the oven, letting it soak in.
Preheat oven to 150°C (300°F) and draw a 9-inch circle on parchment paper as a guide.
Whip egg whites to soft peaks, then gradually add sugar and whip to stiff, glossy peaks.
Fold in cornstarch, vinegar, and vanilla, then mound onto the parchment within the circle, smoothing the sides and creating a slight well in the center.
Bake 60-75 minutes, then turn off the oven and let it cool completely inside with the door closed to prevent cracking.
Top with whipped cream and passionfruit (or other fresh fruit) just before serving.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a square pan. Cream butter and sugar, beat in eggs, then alternate adding flour/baking powder with milk and vanilla.
Pour into the pan and bake 25-30 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely, then chill — it's easier to cut and dip when cold.
Cut the cooled sponge into squares.
Whisk icing sugar, icing cocoa, and icing milk into a thin chocolate icing.
Dip each square in the icing, letting excess drip off, then roll in desiccated coconut.
Let set on a wire rack before serving.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease three 8-inch pans.
Cream butter and sugar, beat in eggs, then fold in flour, cocoa, and baking powder alternately with milk.
Divide between pans and bake 22-25 minutes. Cool completely.
Drizzle each layer with kirsch, then whip the cream with sugar to soft peaks.
Stack layers with cherries and whipped cream between each, frost the outside, and cover with chocolate shavings and extra cherries.
Warm the milk, dissolve the yeast in it, and let it foam for 10 minutes.
Mix flour, sugar, and salt in a large bowl, add the yeast mixture, eggs, egg yolks, and vanilla, then knead until smooth.
Knead in the butter a little at a time until fully incorporated, then fold in candied peel and raisins.
Place in a tall round mold and proof until doubled, about 3-4 hours.
Bake at 170°C (340°F) for 45-50 minutes until deep golden and a skewer comes out clean; cool upside down to keep its tall shape.
Roll the puff pastry into a log, slice into rounds, and press into a muffin tin to form cups.
Whisk sugar and cornstarch, then whisk in milk, cream, cinnamon stick, and lemon peel; simmer until slightly thickened.
Remove the cinnamon and lemon peel, then whisk the hot mixture into the egg yolks.
Fill the pastry cups with custard and bake at 245°C (475°F) for 15-18 minutes until deeply spotted and caramelized on top.
Cool slightly and dust with cinnamon before serving.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease two 8-inch pans.
Cream butter and sugar until pale and fluffy, beat in eggs one at a time and vanilla.
Fold in flour and baking powder until just combined.
Divide between pans and bake 20-25 minutes until golden and springy. Cool completely.
Spread jam over one layer, top with whipped cream, sandwich with the second layer, and dust with powdered sugar.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a 9-inch springform pan.
Warm the stout and butter together until melted, then whisk in cocoa and sugar.
Whisk in sour cream, eggs, and vanilla, then fold in flour and baking soda.
Pour into the pan and bake 45-50 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat cream cheese, powdered sugar, and cream together and spread over the cooled cake — traditionally left white like the head of a stout.
Preheat oven to 165°C (330°F). Mix crushed biscuits with melted butter and press into a 9-inch springform pan.
Beat cheese and sugar until smooth, then beat in eggs one at a time.
Mix in cornstarch, vanilla, and lemon zest until smooth.
Pour over the crust and bake 60-65 minutes until just set with a slight jiggle in the center.
Cool in the oven with the door ajar, then chill at least 4 hours before slicing.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Whip eggs and sugar until thick and pale, then fold in flour and melted butter.
Spread thin layers of batter on parchment and bake 5-6 minutes each until golden; you'll need 6 layers total.
Beat buttercream butter, powdered sugar, and melted chocolate together into a smooth buttercream.
Stack five layers with buttercream between each and over the outside.
Melt the caramel sugar, pour over the sixth layer, quickly cut into wedges before it hardens, and arrange on top as a garnish.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a baking pan.
Whisk eggs and sugar until pale, then whisk in yogurt and oil.
Fold in flour, semolina, baking powder, and coconut until just combined.
Pour into the pan and bake 30-35 minutes until golden. Meanwhile, simmer syrup sugar, water, and lemon juice into a syrup.
Pour the cooled syrup over the hot cake as soon as it comes out of the oven and let it fully absorb before slicing.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a baking pan.
Whisk eggs and sugar until pale, then whisk in oil.
Fold in flour, ground walnuts, breadcrumbs, baking powder, and cinnamon.
Pour into the pan and bake 35-40 minutes until deep golden. Meanwhile, simmer syrup sugar, water, honey, and cinnamon stick into a syrup.
Pour the warm syrup over the hot cake and let it soak in fully before serving.

substitutions.replacement: not recommended — this recipe relies on almond flour

steps: Boil whole oranges (skin on) for 1.5 hours until very soft, then cool and purée in a food processor, removing seeds.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a 9-inch springform pan.
Whisk eggs and sugar until pale, fold in the orange purée, then almond flour, baking powder, and cardamom.
Pour into the pan and bake 50-55 minutes until golden and set (this cake stays moist — a toothpick may come out slightly damp).
Cool completely in the pan before releasing, as it's delicate while warm.

substitutions.replacement: not recommended — this recipe relies on almond flour

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a 9-inch round pan.
Whisk eggs and sugar until pale, then whisk in yogurt, oil, and rose water.
Fold in almond flour, semolina, baking powder, and cardamom.
Pour into the pan and bake 35-40 minutes until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool, then scatter chopped pistachios and dried rose petals (if available) over the top before serving.
Mix golden syrup, oil, and lye water together, then work in flour to form a smooth dough. Rest 1 hour.
Divide lotus seed paste into portions and wrap each around a salted egg yolk.
Divide the dough into smaller portions, flatten, and wrap around each lotus paste ball, sealing completely.
Press each into a mooncake mold to shape, then place on a lined baking sheet.
Bake at 190°C (375°F) for 5 minutes, cool slightly, brush with egg wash, then bake another 15 minutes until golden.
Preheat oven to 165°C (330°F) and line an 8-inch round pan.
Whip eggs and sugar until thick and pale (ribbon stage), then gently fold in flour.
Fold in milk, oil, and vanilla, then pour into the pan and bake 25-28 minutes. Cool completely.
Whip cream and sugar to stiff peaks. Slice the sponge into three layers.
Stack layers with whipped cream and sliced strawberries between each, then frost the outside smooth and decorate with whole strawberries.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease two 8-inch pans.
Whisk eggs and sugar, then whisk in oil, coconut milk, ube halaya, and ube extract.
Fold in flour and baking powder until just combined.
Divide between pans and bake 28-32 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat frosting butter, powdered sugar, and ube halaya together and frost between layers and over the outside.
Dissolve yeast in a little warm water with a pinch of sugar; let it foam for 10 minutes.
Whisk tapioca starch, rice flour, remaining sugar, and salt together, then whisk in coconut milk, eggs, and pandan extract.
Stir in the yeast mixture and let the batter rest 2 hours until bubbly.
Pour into a greased pan and bake at 200°C (400°F) for 30-35 minutes until deep golden with a honeycomb of holes inside.
Cool before slicing — the texture should be chewy and springy.
Whisk all dry ingredients together, then whisk in coconut milk and salt until smooth. Divide the batter in half and tint one half with pandan juice.
Grease a square pan and steam for 5 minutes to warm it, then pour a thin layer of plain batter and steam 3-4 minutes until set.
Pour a thin layer of the green batter on top and steam another 3-4 minutes; repeat, alternating layers, until the batter is used (traditionally 9 layers).
Steam the final layer for 10 minutes to fully set.
Cool completely before slicing into diamonds — the layers should peel apart slightly when eaten.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) with the broiler available, and grease an 8-inch square pan.
Cream butter and sugar until very light, then beat in condensed milk.
Whisk egg yolks separately until thick, then fold into the butter mixture along with flour and mixed spice.
Pour a very thin layer of batter into the pan and broil 2-3 minutes until golden; repeat, adding thin layers and broiling each, until the batter is used (15-20 layers).
Cool completely before slicing thin — the finished cake should show dozens of fine spiced layers.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease two 8-inch pans.
Whisk flour, cocoa, sugar, and baking powder together, then whisk in eggs, milk, and oil.
Divide between pans and bake 25-28 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely.
Cook condensed milk, frosting cocoa, and frosting butter over low heat, stirring constantly, until thick enough to coat a spoon, about 10 minutes; cool slightly.
Spread the brigadeiro frosting between layers and over the outside, then cover generously with chocolate sprinkles.
Melt base butter, sugar, and cocoa together, whisk in the egg, and cook gently until thickened. Stir in graham crumbs, coconut, and walnuts, then press into a lined 9-inch square pan and chill.
Beat filling butter, custard powder, filling sugar, and filling milk together until smooth and spreadable.
Spread the filling over the chilled base and chill again until firm.
Melt the topping chocolate and butter together, then pour over the filling layer, tilting to cover evenly.
Chill until the chocolate sets, then cut into small bars.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F). Combine flour, butter, egg yolks, and baking powder into a smooth dough.
Divide into 6-8 portions, roll each paper-thin, and bake 6-8 minutes each until golden and crisp.
Stack the baked wafer layers with dulce de leche spread between each.
Whip egg whites and meringue sugar over a double boiler until warm, then whip to stiff, glossy peaks.
Pile the meringue over the top and sides, and lightly torch or broil until golden in spots.
Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Bake each puff pastry sheet between two baking sheets (to keep it flat) for 15-18 minutes until golden and crisp.
Cool the pastry sheets completely, then trim to even rectangles.
Stack the sheets with a generous layer of dulce de leche spread between each.
Dust the top layer heavily with powdered sugar.
Chill at least 1 hour before slicing so the layers hold together cleanly.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a 9-inch square pan.
Cream base butter and base sugar, beat in the egg yolk, then fold in flour and baking powder to form a soft dough. Press into the pan.
Spread raspberry jam evenly over the base.
Whip egg whites to soft peaks, gradually add meringue sugar and whip to stiff peaks, then fold in coconut.
Spread the coconut meringue over the jam layer and bake 30-35 minutes until golden. Cool completely before slicing.

substitutions.replacement: not recommended — this recipe relies on almond flour

steps: Mix almond flour and powdered sugar, then work in egg whites to form a smooth, firm dough. Chill 30 minutes.
Roll the dough into ropes and shape into graduated rings using ring molds (18 rings from largest to smallest).
Bake at 175°C (350°F) for 10-12 minutes until lightly golden; cool completely on the molds.
Whisk the icing egg white, icing sugar, and lemon juice into a stiff royal icing.
Stack the rings from largest to smallest into a tower, piping icing in zigzags between each layer to secure and decorate.

substitutions.replacement: omit, increase flour by the same amount

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease small cylindrical molds (or a muffin tin).
Cream butter and sugar, beat in eggs, rum, and almond extract.
Fold in flour, almond flour, breadcrumbs, and baking powder.
Divide into the molds and bake 20-25 minutes until golden. Cool completely.
Top each cake with a small dollop of raspberry jam surrounded by a thin ring of powdered sugar icing.
